spans.exact_text: Employment can grow while some tasks disappear, and unemployment can remain low even when hiring opportunities weaken in particular occupations.
spans.assessment: Task substitution and complementarity can push labour demand in opposite directions; demand expansion and implementation costs affect the net result. A task mechanism is logically possible but is not a measured net employment or output effect. Unemployment is defined relative to the labour force; employment counts, payroll jobs and population-adjusted rates differ. Changes in participation or multiple jobholding mean an aggregate rate cannot settle foregone hiring or occupation-specific losses. Vacancies are an unfilled-position stock, while hires and separations are period flows. A fall can follow weaker demand or changed matching and does not by itself identify redundancies, AI substitution or easier recruitment. Occupational counts depend on survey concepts and classification membership. Two related occupation labels can cover different workers; reconciling the crosswalk is necessary before treating their level gap as substantive disagreement.

spans.exact_text: Hiring, employment, unemployment and pay should not be interchanged.

spans.exact_text: Chip prices, hosting contracts, electricity tariffs and commodity prices describe different parts of the cost environment.
spans.assessment: Local grid and connection constraints can differ from national average tariffs. A price, a power rating and metered energy are different quantities, and fuel/network/contract conditions can change them without an AI-specific demand shock. A traded input price does not reveal the quantity or expenditure share attributable to computing facilities. Other industries, supply conditions and financial demand remain uncontrolled; the series is cost context, not verified construction or an AI-demand estimate. A published semiconductor basket and a quality-adjusted microprocessor comparison do not equal current GPU performance per dollar. Historical matched-model bias motivates checking quality methods but cannot supply a corrected present-day index. Hosting, applications and software-development contracts purchase different services. Index rebasing only rescales a series; constant-quality cost per AI task requires a matched benchmark, product coverage and quality method.
